questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had always dreamed of goint to Australia and this was just the perfect opportunity. It was also a plus that Australia is an English speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic opportunities were not that many but the personal growth and experience was worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy most of the information was sent by email and the international department is pretty extensive. All crucial information was sent or easily accesible but there was some "good-to-know" information that you had to know to look for to get. You have to find your way to your recidence yourself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first week (o-week) had a bunch of information events and a mandatory information event for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a bit overwhelming having to find everything but as long as you turn up or look for it you get all the information and assistance you need.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They have a host of different recidence halls (kollegier) and you are guaranteed a room in one of these as long as you apply before a certain deadline.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Some of the halls are fully catered the rest have small kitchens where recidents can cook food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is great and you'll meet a lot of new people but it is also loud.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to find the courses you want to take and then nominate them before getting an offer letter. If the courses have prerequisites you also have to prove that you meet those in your nomination. However it is possible (and as far as I heard relatively easy) to change courses after getting to the university by talking to the student admin.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You are pretty much on your own when having to select courses but you can always contact the student admin, and it is possible to talk to student admin about changing or swapping courses as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my first priority courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Select the courses you want from the start but don't stress it because you have time to change them later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one first year, two second year and one third year courses. I would say the level is just slightly below the level of courses at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much the same although all lectures were recorded and one of my courses was a flipped classroom.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ASTR1003: Astronomy and Space
BIOL2202: Experiments and Analysis in Biology
PSYC2007: Biological Basis of Behaviour
NEUR3112: Systems Neuroscience

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking a first year course in a topic that interests you as a "buffer" course you maybe put a bit less effort into. Having four courses at the same time is a lot of work if you are putting in max effort in all of them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A room changing fee.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most were the same as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were quite a few clubs and sport opportunities but they were all pretty expensive / cost money.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some smaller events by the student comittee.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You can get free gym-classes through the student comittee those are a great opportunity to do sport and meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get outside! If you are able go for hikes on the mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy it's not that different from here.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If living on campus mingle in the dinning hall people are generally very welcomming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Perhaps just having to speak another language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are generally very open, welcomming and laid back.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Meeting new people is the real experience, live in a hall of in a share.
2. Get outside as often as you can.
3. Ask for help, it's there as long as you ask for it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything I can think off at the moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Hiking up a proper mountain and laughing in the dinning hall.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to share a space with other people and juggling four courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
